prompt: Explain gerrymandering using only golf metaphors. Keep going after the metaphor files a complaint.
response:
Imagine you and your rival are playing an 18-hole match play tournament at the local country club. You wear the Red polo; your opponent wears the Blue polo. In match play, whoever wins the most holes wins the election—I mean, the trophy. 

But there’s a catch: you are also the head greenskeeper, and the club’s charter lets you move the tee boxes, the greens, and the out-of-bounds stakes the night before the tournament to decide what constitutes a "hole." 

To guarantee your Red polo wins, you employ two specific course-design strategies. 

The first is called "Packing the Hazards." You look at all the terrain where the Blue player excels—let's say they're great at hitting out of the sand and playing over water. You redraw the stakes so that 90% of the course’s sand traps and lakes are aggressively crammed into a single, winding, monstrosity of a Par 8. You fully concede that hole. The Blue player will absolutely crush you on Hole 4. But by dumping all their favorable terrain into one single bucket, you’ve left the remaining 17 holes as flat, hazard-free, 100-yard chip-and-putts perfectly tailored to your Red polo game. Blue wins one hole by ten strokes; you win seventeen holes by one stroke. 

The second strategy is "Cracking the Fairways." Let’s say the Blue player has a massive, booming drive that always lands in a specific valley. You take the lawn paint and carve that valley up, dividing it across the boundaries of six different holes. Now, whenever Blue hits their signature drive, their ball lands just inside the rough of someone else’s fairway. Their advantage is diluted across the front nine, ensuring they never have quite enough favorable lies to win a single one of those holes outright.

***

*[DING. A formal grievance has been lodged by the Golf Metaphor.]*

**GOLF METAPHOR:** "Excuse me, I am filing an official complaint with the Literary USGA. This is a gross violation of analogy etiquette. You cannot just redraw a fairway in the dead of night! What about the sprinkler systems? What about the gentlemanly integrity of the sport?! No club would ever allow a player to act as the architect *while* they are on the scorecard. This comparison is preposterous and I demand to be retired back to the clubhouse immediately before you mention a 'handicap.'"

***

Request denied. Grab your 9-iron, we are playing through. 

As I was saying before the concept of golf objected, this greenskeeping manipulation completely ruins the integrity of the scorecard. Because of this strategic landscaping, the Red polo can shoot a disastrous 115 across the whole day, yet still walk away with the championship because the course was mapped to hide their shanks and amplify the Blue polo's bogeys. 

Furthermore, this creates the ultimate "Incumbent Mulligan." Because the Red greenskeeper knows exactly how the weird, snake-shaped fairways bend, no rookie challenger will ever learn the breaks on the green well enough to beat them. The tournament is decided before anyone even takes their first practice swing, simply because the guy keeping the score is the same guy who planted the flags.
